title: A Separate People as to Their Faith
summary: Many of the rising generation could not understand King Benjamin’s words; they had been little children when he spoke to his people. They did not believe their fathers’ tradition or what had been said concerning the resurrection of the dead and the coming of Christ. Because of their unbelief, they could not understand the word of God. They would not be baptized, join the church, or call upon the Lord their God. They were a separate people as to their faith and remained so.

explicit_facts.text: Many of the rising generation could not understand King Benjamin’s words. They had been little children when he spoke to his people, and they did not believe the tradition of their fathers.
They did not believe what had been said concerning the resurrection of the dead or the coming of Christ.
Because of their unbelief, they could not understand the word of God, and their hearts were hardened.
They would not be baptized, join the church, or call upon the Lord their God. They were a separate people as to their faith and remained so ever after, in their carnal and sinful state.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A group of people can represent the rising generation without depicting a particular refusal as it happens.
unspecified_visual_details: Their exact number, ages, clothing, and surroundings are not specified.

narration.text: And they were a separate people as to their faith, and remained so ever after, even in their carnal and sinful state;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses report beliefs and refusals; they do not narrate a particular debate or baptism encounter.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict King Benjamin speaking as a current event.
Do not invent dialogue, a baptism attempt, a visible resurrection, or an appearance of Christ.

title: Dissension and Admonishment
summary: During Mosiah’s reign, the group referred to as “they” was not half so numerous as the people of God, but became more numerous because of dissensions among the brethren. They deceived many people in the church with flattering words and caused them to commit many sins. It became expedient for the church to admonish those members who sinned.

explicit_facts.text: During Mosiah’s reign, the group referred to as “they” was not half so numerous as the people of God, but became more numerous because of dissensions among the brethren.
They deceived many people in the church with flattering words and caused them to commit many sins.
It became expedient for the church to admonish those members who sinned.

unspecified_visual_details: The groups’ individual identities and appearances are unspecified.
The location and the content of the flattering words are unspecified.

narration.text: but because of the dissensions among the brethren they became more numerous.
they did deceive many with their flattering words
it became expedient that those who committed sin, that were in the church, should be admonished by the church.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Narration-only treatment: these verses summarize developments rather than depict a specific encounter or an admonishment taking place.
The people of God, the brethren, and church members are group categories, not individually identified characters.
prohibited_inventions: Do not stage a particular persuasive speech, act of sin, or admonishment.
Do not invent flattering words or identify the group referred to as “they” beyond these verses.
Do not portray the group categories as distinct named or biographical characters.

title: Brought Before Alma
summary: Teachers delivered them to the priests, who brought them before Alma. King Mosiah had given Alma authority over the church. Many people stood and testified against them.
characters: People who were brought before Alma

explicit_facts.text: Teachers delivered them to the priests, and the priests brought them before Alma, the high priest.
King Mosiah had given Alma authority over the church.
Alma did not know concerning them.
Many witnesses stood and testified against them concerning their iniquity.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The people brought before Alma, the priests, and the witnesses may be shown together.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, the identities of those brought before Alma, and the specific iniquities are not stated.

narration.text: and the priests brought them before Alma, who was the high priest.
Now king Mosiah had given Alma the authority over the church.
yea, the people stood and testified of their iniquity in abundance.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Mosiah's grant of authority is prior context, not an event occurring during the appearance before Alma.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict King Mosiah as present.
Do not invent specific charges, testimony, or a formal court setting.

title: Alma Brings the Matter to Mosiah
summary: Troubled because this situation was unprecedented in the church, Alma brought the accused before King Mosiah and asked him to judge them. Mosiah replied that he did not judge them and delivered them into Alma’s hands to be judged.

explicit_facts.text: Because no such thing had happened before in the church, Alma was troubled and caused the accused to be brought before the king.
Alma told the king that the accused had been taken in iniquities, did not repent, and had been brought for judgment according to their crimes.
Mosiah said he did not judge them and delivered them into Alma’s hands to be judged.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and the accused may be shown before Mosiah during the exchange.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, arrangement of those present, and any visible marks of Alma’s distress are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, here are many whom we have brought before thee, who are accused of their brethren; yea, and they have been taken in divers iniquities.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (the Younger) (high priest)

spoken_dialogue.text: And they do not repent of their iniquities; therefore we have brought them before thee, that thou mayest judge them according to their crimes.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Alma (the Younger) (high priest)

spoken_dialogue.text: Behold, I judge them not; therefore I deliver them into thy hands to be judged.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: King Mosiah II (king)

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Keep Alma’s appeal and Mosiah’s response in this exchange, not combined with Alma’s later inquiry to the Lord.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a verdict by Mosiah; he returns the matter to Alma.

title: Alma Inquires of the Lord
summary: Alma was again troubled and went to inquire of the Lord what to do, fearing he might do wrong in God’s sight. After pouring out his whole soul to God, he heard the Lord’s voice.

explicit_facts.text: Alma was troubled again, went to inquire of the Lord what he should do, and feared doing wrong in God’s sight.
After Alma poured out his whole soul to God, the voice of the Lord came to him.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown alone in prayer; the text does not specify the setting.
unspecified_visual_details: The place, Alma’s posture, and any visible manifestation accompanying the voice are not specified.

narration.text: And it came to pass that after he had poured out his whole soul to God, the voice of the Lord came to him, saying:

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord is heard as a voice; no visible form is described.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict a visible divine figure or add sensory effects for the voice.

title: Blessings Spoken to Alma
summary: A speaker blesses Alma and the people, speaks of the church Alma established and Alma’s inquiry concerning the transgressor, and covenants eternal life to Alma.

explicit_facts.text: Alma and those baptized in the waters of Mormon are blessed; Alma is blessed for his faith in Abinadi’s words.
The people are blessed for their faith in Alma’s words.
Alma has established a church among the people; the speaker says they shall be established and shall be his people.
The people willing to bear the speaker’s name are blessed.
Alma is blessed because he inquired concerning the transgressor.
The speaker calls Alma his servant, covenants eternal life to him, and says Alma will serve him, go forth in his name, and gather his sheep.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma may be shown listening without showing the speaker.
unspecified_visual_details: Alma’s appearance and the location are not described.
The speaker’s appearance is not described; the other people mentioned are not stated to be present.

spoken_dialogue.text: Thou art blessed because of thy exceeding faith in the words alone of my servant Abinadi.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: And blessed are they because of their exceeding faith
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: and they shall be established, and they shall be my people.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: I covenant with thee that thou shalt have eternal life;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

spoken_dialogue.text: and thou shalt serve me and go forth in my name, and shalt gather together my sheep.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: Unidentified speaker

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The supplied verses do not explicitly name the speaker.
The baptisms, establishment of the church, and Alma’s inquiry are referred to as past events; gathering the sheep is stated as future action.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the baptisms, the founding of the church, the inquiry, or the gathering of sheep as happening during this speech.
Do not give the speaker a visible form or identify Alma as Alma the Younger from these verses alone.
Do not depict literal sheep solely from the speaker’s figurative charge.

title: The Church and the Promise
summary: The Lord speaks of receiving people into his church, baptism unto repentance, forgiveness, and a place at his right hand.

explicit_facts.text: The Lord says those who hear his voice are his sheep, are to be received into the church, and will also be received by him.
The Lord calls the church his, says baptism is unto repentance, and says he will forgive those received who believe in his name.
The Lord says he takes upon himself the sins of the world and grants a place at his right hand to one who believes to the end.
The Lord says those called in his name who know him shall come forth and have a place eternally at his right hand.

unspecified_visual_details: The Lord's appearance and the setting are not specified.

spoken_dialogue.text: And he that will hear my voice shall be my sheep;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: whosoever is baptized shall be baptized unto repentance.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and it is I that granteth unto him that believeth unto the end a place at my right hand.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: and if they know me they shall come forth, and shall have a place eternally at my right hand.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The sheep and the place at the Lord's right hand are teachings here, not narrated visible events.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict literal sheep or a heavenly place.
Do not invent the Lord's appearance, a listener, or a setting.

title: The Lord’s Teaching on the Last Day
summary: The Lord says that when the second trump sounds, those who never knew him will come forth and stand before him. They will know him as their God and Redeemer, but would not be redeemed. He says he will confess that he never knew them, and they will depart into everlasting fire. He instructs that those who will not hear his voice are not to be received into his church, and he will not receive them at the last day.

explicit_facts.text: When the second trump sounds, those who never knew the Lord will come forth and stand before him.
They will know him as their God and Redeemer, but would not be redeemed.
The Lord will confess that he never knew them, and they will depart into everlasting fire prepared for the devil and his angels.
Those who will not hear his voice are not to be received into his church, and he will not receive them at the last day.

unspecified_visual_details: The Lord’s visible appearance and the setting of this teaching are not described.
The appearance of the future judgment is not described.

spoken_dialogue.text: when the second trump shall sound
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: I am the Lord their God, that I am their Redeemer; but they would not be redeemed.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: I never knew them; and they shall depart into everlasting fire
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: he that will not hear my voice, the same shall ye not receive into my church
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The Lord speaks of future judgment; these verses do not narrate it as occurring during the teaching.
prohibited_inventions: Do not depict the future judgment as presently occurring.
Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord or depict the devil or his angels as present.
Do not invent an addressee or setting.

title: Instructions on Repentance and Forgiveness
summary: The speaker gives instructions about judging transgressors, forgiving those who confess and sincerely repent, forgiving one another, and not numbering the unrepentant among the speaker’s people.

explicit_facts.text: The speaker instructs the addressees to judge transgressors according to their sins and forgive those who confess and sincerely repent; the speaker also promises forgiveness.
The speaker promises to forgive the people’s trespasses as often as they repent.
The speaker instructs the addressees to forgive one another and says that refusing to forgive a neighbor who says they repent brings condemnation.
The speaker says that those who will not repent shall not be numbered among the speaker’s people from that time forward.

reasonable_visual_inferences: The instructions could be conveyed as speech without depicting the speaker or addressees.
unspecified_visual_details: The speaker’s and addressees’ appearances are unspecified.

spoken_dialogue.text: him shall ye judge according to the sins which he has committed;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: him shall ye forgive, and I will forgive him also.
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: as often as my people repent will I forgive them
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: And ye shall also forgive one another your trespasses;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

spoken_dialogue.text: whosoever will not repent of his sins the same shall not be numbered among my people;
spoken_dialogue.speaker: The Lord

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These verses give instructions about judgment, repentance, forgiveness, and who is numbered among the speaker’s people; they do not narrate an example of those instructions being carried out.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a visible appearance for the Lord or the addressees.
Do not invent a transgressor, confession, forgiveness exchange, or exclusion event.

title: Alma Records the Words
summary: After hearing the Lord’s words, Alma wrote them down so he could judge the church’s people according to God’s commandments. He then went and judged those who had been taken in iniquity according to the Lord’s word.

explicit_facts.text: Alma wrote down the Lord’s words so he could judge the people of the church according to God’s commandments.
Alma went and judged those taken in iniquity according to the word of the Lord.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma writing may be shown as the first moment; his judging the accused is a subsequent moment and should not be combined in one image.
unspecified_visual_details: The writing material, setting, and procedure of judgment are not stated.

narration.text: And it came to pass when Alma had heard these words he wrote them down

doctrinal_or_story_notes: These are two successive actions; depict the writing, not a composite of writing and judgment.
prohibited_inventions: Do not show the Lord physically dictating or add a specific judgment procedure.

title: Alma Judges the Accused
summary: Alma judged those taken in iniquity according to the Lord’s word. He numbered those who confessed and repented among the church, while those who would not confess and repent were not numbered, and their names were blotted out.

explicit_facts.text: Alma judged those taken in iniquity according to the word of the Lord.
Alma numbered those who repented and confessed their sins among the church people.
Those who would not confess and repent were not numbered among the church people, and their names were blotted out.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and the accused may be shown during the judgment; the outcomes can be conveyed through a written record.
unspecified_visual_details: The exact process, whether the people appeared together, and the form of the record are not stated.

narration.text: And whosoever repented of their sins and did confess them, them he did number among the people of the church;
And those that would not confess their sins and repent of their iniquity, the same were not numbered among the people of the church, and their names were blotted out.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: Confession and repentance distinguish the two reported outcomes.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent the people’s words, particular sins, or a written list design.

title: Peace and Growth in the Church
summary: Alma regulated the affairs of the church. They began again to have peace and prosper in church affairs, walking circumspectly before God, receiving many, and baptizing many.

explicit_facts.text: Alma regulated all the affairs of the church.
They began again to have peace and to prosper exceedingly in church affairs.
They walked circumspectly before God, received many, and baptized many.

reasonable_visual_inferences: A general depiction of church life could suggest peace and growth without presenting the summarized activities as one simultaneous event.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, church administration, and identities of those received or baptized are not stated.

narration.text: And it came to pass that Alma did regulate all the affairs of the church; and they began again to have peace and to prosper exceedingly in the affairs of the church, walking circumspectly before God, receiving many, and baptizing many.

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verse summarizes conditions and activities; it does not place them all in one instant.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent a particular convert, baptismal location, administrative action, or simultaneous gathering.

title: Alma and His Fellow Laborers
summary: Alma and his fellow laborers over the church diligently taught the word of God, suffered afflictions, and were persecuted by those outside the church. They admonished their brethren, were themselves admonished by the word of God according to their sins, and were commanded to pray without ceasing and give thanks in all things.
characters: His fellow laborers over the church
Those who did not belong to the church of God

explicit_facts.text: Alma and his fellow laborers were over the church, taught the word of God, suffered afflictions, and were persecuted by those who did not belong to the church of God.
They admonished their brethren and were themselves admonished by the word of God according to their sins; they were commanded to pray without ceasing and give thanks in all things.

reasonable_visual_inferences: Alma and his fellow laborers may be depicted teaching, without specifying what they said.
unspecified_visual_details: The location, individual laborers, particular afflictions, and acts of persecution are not described.

narration.text: And they did admonish their brethren;

doctrinal_or_story_notes: The verses describe ongoing activities, not a particular confrontation or a specific prayer.
prohibited_inventions: Do not invent an attack, a specific prayer, or words spoken in teaching or admonishment.
